The direction and qualified relation match the source: The destruction and exhaustion of militant organization before Germinal impaired the rising. Rebind from the post-Prairial repression unit, which occurs later and cannot cause Germinal’s failure.

The direction and qualified relation match the source: Factional conflict culminated in the coercive purge on 2 June; the Commission of Twelve was an earlier defensive step, not itself the final event.
The direction and qualified relation match the source: Chaumette linked municipal provisioning failure to the September mobilization; he did not command all popular actors.
Page262 supports Robespierre’s resistance to atheistic coercion;276 supports the civic cult. Page264 is administrative recall context.

The direction and qualified relation match the source: Destruction of popular rivals transferred control to government while Terror grew harsher; do not treat the Commune purge as termination of terror.

The direction and qualified relation match the source: Separation withdrew state payment for religion, including civic worship; this is a fiscal and institutional ending of official support, not an assertion that private belief vanished.

The direction and qualified relation match the source: Chaumette’s eventual execution and the purge of the Commune followed his guarded response to insurrection; avoid labeling him an unqualified organizer of Hébert’s failed rising.
The direction and qualified relation match the source: The post-coup dismantling included repeal of 22 Prairial; the earlier law’s enactment and social effects are separate requirements.
